requirement_title: Feature Request: Allow generation of Formatter for a type in a referenced assembly
requirement_text:
# REQ-2129: Feature Request: Allow generation of Formatter for a type in a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2129
Type: feature

## Requirement

Given Project A (contains `ProjectA.MyType`, has no and cannot have a reference to the MessagePack NuGet package) and Project B (references Project A and MessagePack), the reporter needs a source-generated `IMessagePackFormatter` for `ProjectA.MyType` generated inside Project B.

Proposed solution: add a `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute that works for partial classes implementing `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`:

```csharp
[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]
partial class MyObjectFormatter: IMessagePackFormatter<MyObject>;
```

The class does not need a body; the implementation is source-generated by `MessagePack.SourceGenerator.MessagePackGenerator` as usual.

For attribute-based property keys and other settings (such as Union), the issue lists three alternatives: (1) use `System.Runtime.Serialization.DataMember` and related attributes; (2) let the generator and analyzers work with user-defined copies of the MessagePack attributes; (3) source-generate the attributes themselves via `RegisterPostInitializationOutput`.

Motivation: Project A is a NuGet library that should stay minimal with zero dependencies.

## Acceptance criteria

- A `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute exists and can be applied to a partial class implementing `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`.
- The source generator emits the formatter implementation for `T` inside the annotated class, in the assembly that declares the class (Project B), even when `T` is declared in a referenced assembly.
- The annotated class may be declared without a body (`partial class X : IMessagePackFormatter<T>;`).
- `T` needs no MessagePack attributes: without `[DataContract]` or `[MessagePackObject]` on `T` the generated formatter uses contractless behaviour over public members. (derived from maintainer comment)
- If `T` does carry MessagePack attributes, they are honoured. (derived from maintainer comment)
- Private members are not required to be serialized; only public members are in scope. (derived from maintainer comment)
- Project A needs no reference to the MessagePack package. (derived)

## Notes from discussion

- AArnott: "We might simplistically say this only works in 'contractless' mode, such that you need no attributes on it at all. If there are attributes on it, fine, we'll use them. But if there is no `[DataContract]` or `[MessagePackObject]` attribute on the type, go contractless by default."
- AArnott on prerequisite: "Does ProjectA.MyType requires only `public` members to be serialized? That seems a prerequisite for anything here." Reporter: yes.
- AArnott is not a fan of a `PropertyKeys` dictionary on the formatter, and warns that copying attributes into Project A breaks reflection-based (dynamic resolver) mode.
- AArnott suggested a surrogate-type design: `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter(SurrogateType = typeof(ProjectASurrogate))]`, keys mapped by property name; reporter: "Looks good." No design was settled in the thread.

findings.claim: When no surrogate is specified, the collector always builds a contractless string-key model and never examines attributes on the formatted type. Consequently, MessagePack attributes such as [Key] and [IgnoreMember] on T are ignored—for example, an [IgnoreMember] property is serialized and an integer [Key(7)] is replaced by the property-name string key—contrary to the acceptance criterion that attributes on T are honoured.

receipt_plan.detail: Run the generated test MessagePackAttributesOnReferencedTypeAreHonored. It compiles a referenced type with [MessagePackObject], [Key(7)] on Id, and [IgnoreMember] on Secret, then requires the generated formatter to write key 7 and not access Secret. The current contractless implementation fails both assertions.

hunches.claim: MsgPack020 and its documentation require exactly one IMessagePackFormatter<T> interface, but the collector rejects only zero interfaces. A formatter implementing two such interfaces silently uses formatterInterfaces[0], producing a formatter for an arbitrarily selected data type instead of the documented error.

receipt_plan.detail: Add a generator test with an annotated partial class implementing both IMessagePackFormatter<FirstType> and IMessagePackFormatter<SecondType>. Assert MsgPack020 and no generated formatter body. The current Length == 0 check produces neither the required diagnostic nor a deterministic rejection.

hunches.claim: MessagePack attributes on the formatted type are never inspected. With no surrogate, every attributed type is sent through CreateContractlessMembers, so [Key] values are replaced by alphabetic string keys and [IgnoreMember] members are serialized, contrary to the acceptance criterion that attributes on T be honoured.

receipt_plan.detail: Generate a user-declared formatter for a [MessagePackObject] type having one [Key] property and one [IgnoreMember] property. Inspect the generated partial formatter: it must exclude the ignored member and use the declared key. On head, the generated formatter contains serialization/deserialization code for the ignored member.

hunches.claim: A formatter implementing IMessagePackFormatter<T> for two different data types is accepted even though MsgPack020 describes the exactly-one-data-type requirement. Only the zero-interface case is rejected; formatterInterfaces[0] is then chosen arbitrarily, leaving the other interface unimplemented and causing compiler errors in the generated compilation instead of MsgPack020.

receipt_plan.detail: Run the generator over a [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] partial class implementing both IMessagePackFormatter<A> and IMessagePackFormatter<B>. Assert that generator diagnostics contain MsgPack020. Head emits no such diagnostic.

hunches.claim: The partial validation checks only the annotated class itself. A partial formatter nested in a non-partial containing class passes collection, but the generator cannot add another declaration of that nested type without also extending its container. The resulting generated compilation has conflicting/missing-partial type declarations (and the original formatter may remain unimplemented) rather than being supported or rejected with MsgPack019.

receipt_plan.detail: Run the generator for public class Outer containing a [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] public partial class NestedFormatter : IMessagePackFormatter<Poco>. The collector should reject this layout with MsgPack019 unless it can generate every containing declaration compatibly. Head reports no MsgPack019 because IsPartial examines only NestedFormatter.

hunches.claim: The generator always uses contractless members when no surrogate is supplied, so MessagePack attributes on an external formatted type are not honoured. For example, an external [MessagePackObject] type with [Key(0)] and [IgnoreMember] members will instead be serialized as a string-keyed map containing every public read-write member.

receipt_plan.detail: Add an external type annotated with [MessagePackObject], an integer [Key] on one public property, and [IgnoreMember] on another; generate its formatter without SurrogateType, round-trip it, and inspect the serialized bytes. The accepted behaviour requires the integer-keyed array and omitted ignored member, whereas this implementation produces contractless string keys and includes the ignored member.

hunches.claim: The required behaviour of honouring existing MessagePack attributes on T has no test: every external test type is attribute-free. The unconditional contractless branch can therefore ignore [MessagePackObject]/[Key] on T without any test failing, and a wire-format test for such a type would currently expose that gap.

receipt_plan.detail: Add an external type marked [MessagePackObject] with members keyed differently from contractless order (for example [Key(5)] public int Id and [IgnoreMember] on another public property), generate its formatter without a surrogate, and assert integer-key array serialization and round-trip. The test should fail against the shown unconditional CreateContractlessMembers path.

hunches.claim: No test uses the explicitly supported semicolon/bodyless declaration form; all attributed formatters have braced bodies. A regression that recognizes only ordinary braced formatter declarations would leave this acceptance criterion untested.

receipt_plan.detail: Add a compilation/execution test declaring '[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] public partial class ExternalPointFormatter : IMessagePackFormatter<ExternalPoint>;' with no braces, then resolve the formatter and round-trip an ExternalPoint.

hunches.claim: The public-field portion of contractless member selection is untested because ExternalPerson, ExternalPoint, and ExternalWidget expose only properties. Losing all fields from generated contracts would not be noticed.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs:283 swap-boolean: 'IFieldSymbol field => field.DeclaredAccessibility == Accessibility.Public && !field.IsReadOnly && !field.IsConst' -> 'IFieldSymbol field => false'; expected to survive because every generated-formatter execution fixture uses properties rather than public fields

hunches.claim: The accessible parameterless-constructor requirement has no negative test; all formatted classes have usable constructors and the only rejected-data-type test covers abstractness.

hunches.claim: Successful surrogate generation is tested only with integer keys. There is no assertion that a string [Key] on a surrogate controls the emitted map key, so ignoring the explicit string key would pass the suite.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs:210 delete-statement: 'CreateMember(target, intKey: members.Count, stringKey: (string)key)' -> 'CreateMember(target, intKey: members.Count, stringKey: target.Name)'; expected to survive because the only successful surrogate execution test uses integer keys, while the string-key unit input is rejected for mixing key kinds

hunches.claim: Duplicate surrogate keys are not covered by any diagnostic test, allowing two members to claim the same wire key if the uniqueness check regresses.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs:202 remove-guard: 'if (!claimedKeys.Add(key))' -> 'if (false)'; expected to survive because all successful surrogate keys are unique and no test expects MsgPack007 for duplicate surrogate keys

hunches.claim: suppressed by unconfirmed context entry: [L11] area=analyzer, generator: Types that come from a referenced assembly are deliberately not analysed and get no formatter from the compiling assembly. In `TypeCollector.CollectCore`, after the custom-formatter, enum and generic checks, a non-generic type whose symbol is metadata-only exits with a bare `if (type.Locations[0].IsInMetadata) { return; }` (TypeCollector.cs:367-370), so no MsgPack003/004/005 diagnostic and no generated formatter appear for it. The defining assembly owns validating and formatting its own types (rationale inferred: the code has no comment). A missing diagnostic or formatter for such a type is not a defect. (source: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:367) (would-be finding: Generating a formatter for a metadata-only type is an explicit opt-in exception to the existing ownership rule, rather than an accidental violation: only formatter classes annotated in the compiling assembly enter this new collector, while ordinary referenced types remain uncollected.)

receipt_plan.detail: [L11] records that referenced-assembly types deliberately receive no formatter or analysis from the compiling assembly. This feature preserves that default and adds the requirement's explicit [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] opt-in path, so the metadata-type exemption should not be flagged as a defect.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Add the marker attribute with an optional SurrogateType property so Project B can supply MessagePack-specific keys and settings on a surrogate type mapped to T by property name. Code: In addition to basic formatter generation, the generator must resolve and validate the surrogate, read its MessagePack annotations, and apply them to T's corresponding properties; the attribute gains a public Type-valued SurrogateType surface.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: Add only the marker attribute and generate a bodyless partial formatter, using contractless public-member serialization by default and honoring DataContract or MessagePack metadata already present on T, without adding any new configuration mechanism. Code: The public API contains GeneratedMessagePackFormatterAttribute without SurrogateType; key and union customization is limited to metadata already on T (including DataMember and related attributes), and user-defined attribute copies receive no special recognition.
